paper_metadata.title: Quantum Circuit-Based Adaptation for Credit Risk Analysis

summary: The paper experimentally demonstrates hardware-aware variational loading of discrete Gaussian distributions on a superconducting QPU: a 2-qubit circuit on D3-C4 with optimal theta1 = 237° and a 3-qubit circuit on D3-A6-C4 with optimal angles theta1 = 212.5° and theta2 = 104.5°. It then uses these loaders inside a 3-qubit credit-risk GCI circuit, reporting that the experimental and simulated CDFs agree within about 5% and place the 95% VaR at total loss L = 1000, with P(L <= 0) ≈ 0.75 and P(L <= 1000) = 1.0.

experiments.description: Hardware-aware preparation of a two-qubit discrete Gaussian distribution on a superconducting QPU, used as the latent-factor loading subcircuit for credit-risk analysis.

algorithm.variant: hardware-aware variational quantum circuit for discrete normal distribution loading
algorithm.ansatz: 2-qubit hardware-efficient ansatz with single-qubit Ry rotations and one entangler (CNOT implemented via native CZ)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained until the output histogram matched the target discrete Gaussian; no explicit stopping threshold reported
algorithm.parameter_initialization: theta0 fixed to 90°; theta1 initialized from prior software optimization and then swept/fine-tuned on hardware

problem_formulation.encoding_details: two qubits encode a 4-point discretization of a standard normal distribution over the latent factor z; basis states map to discrete z values
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize squared distance between measured probabilities p_b(theta) and target histogram p*_b for a discrete Gaussian

problem_instance.description: Discrete Gaussian loading for a one-factor credit-risk latent variable model

dataset_specification.description: standard normal distribution used as target for the latent factor register

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: affine mapping from basis index to grid points z(b) in [-zmax, zmax]
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: hardware experiments with repeated measurements; 100 repeated measurements used for error bars; comparison against Gaussian fit and simulated target

hardware.transpilation_target: superconducting backend with native CZ and hardware-aware routing

implementation_details.transpilation_target: QPU coupling map / native CZ basis

transpilation_settings.routing_method: SABRE (for the GCI circuit; this Gaussian-loading experiment is hardware-tuned directly)

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: classical target-histogram fitting and parameter optimization with Adam

speedup_claims.caveats: No quantum speedup claim; the experiment is a hardware-aware proof-of-concept for distribution loading.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No advantage resources demonstrated; only a 2-qubit proof-of-concept Gaussian-loading subcircuit on a superconducting QPU
limiting_factors: classical baseline is only a target histogram fit, not a hard computational benchmark

notes: Two-qubit Gaussian-loading experiment on D3-C4 pair; optimal theta1=237° reported in main text. Circuit depth not explicitly stated, but the circuit is a single entangling layer with two Ry gates and one CNOT.
The paper reports agreement with a classical Gaussian target and does not claim quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Hardware-aware implementation of the one-factor Gaussian Conditional Independence (GCI) credit-risk circuit on a superconducting QPU, including a Gaussian latent-factor loader and an asset-conditional rotation subcircuit.

algorithm.variant: hardware-aware transpiled GCI circuit with variational tuning of Gaussian-loader and asset-rotation angles
algorithm.ansatz: hybrid circuit composed of a 2-qubit Gaussian loader plus conditional asset-rotation block; transpiled with Qiskit preset pass manager and SABRE routing
algorithm.convergence_criteria: hardware-tuned to match the classical CDF/VaR on the chosen grid; no explicit stopping threshold reported
algorithm.parameter_initialization: initial angles derived from noiseless classical/quantum optimization, then re-tuned on hardware; Gaussian-loader subcircuit replaced by experimentally optimized 2-qubit loader

problem_formulation.encoding_details: three qubits total: two qubits encode the latent Gaussian factor and one qubit encodes the asset default probability; bitstrings are postprocessed into latent-variable and default components
problem_formulation.objective_function: estimate the loss CDF and 95% VaR for a one-asset GCI credit-risk model
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: conditional rotations and transpilation to hardware-native gates; no explicit penalty formulation

problem_instance.description: One-asset, one-factor credit-risk analysis instance under the Gaussian conditional-independence model

dataset_specification.description: baseline default probability p0=0.25, correlation rho=0.027, latent factor Z~N(0,1)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: measured bitstrings are split into latent-factor bits and default bits; latent bits are converted to integer indices to accumulate P(Z=z); default bits determine scenario losses and LGD aggregation; identical losses are collapsed to form PDF/CDF
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: comparison of experimental CDF against simulated transpiled circuits; 95% VaR comparison; 100 repeated measurements for error bars

hardware.transpilation_target: hardware-aware transpilation to native CZ basis with SABRE routing and preset pass manager

implementation_details.transpilation_target: Qiskit preset pass manager on the target backend; native CZ basis; SABRE mapping/routing
implementation_details.classical_solver: classical CDF/VaR postprocessing from measured bitstrings
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: classical optimization of Gaussian-loader angles; transpilation and replacement of a subcircuit with experimentally tuned hardware-ready loader
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: bitstring-to-loss mapping, PDF/CDF construction, VaR extraction

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical CDF/VaR postprocessing and noiseless simulation
speedup_claims.conditions: for the specific one-asset, one-factor GCI instance on the tested grid
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports agreement with the classical/simulated baseline, not a speedup. It states the 95% VaR matches at loss L=1000 and the CDF values coincide at the observed points.

notes: GCI experiment uses the D3-A6-C4 register and a transpiled circuit with a replaced Gaussian-loading subcircuit. The paper reports the use of Qiskit preset pass manager and SABRE, but not an explicit circuit depth or gate count.

experiments.description: Two-qubit Gaussian distribution loading on the A6-D3 register, including the control/target-directionality study and counter-phase correction for the CNOT decomposition.

algorithm.variant: hardware-aware variational quantum circuit for discrete normal distribution loading
algorithm.ansatz: 2-qubit hardware-efficient ansatz with single-qubit Ry rotations and one entangler (CNOT via native CZ)

key_results: Optimal angle combination reported as theta0 = 90° and theta1 = 224° for the A6-D3 pair in the main text
Supplementary Sec. IX.A reports theta1 = 222° for the A6-D3 register in an alternative run
CZ interleaved randomized benchmarking for A6-D3 gives FCZ, IRB = 0.9969 ± 0.0022
A counter-phase Rz gate of -135° is used to correct the CNOTD3,A6 implementation

experiments.description: Hardware-ready transpiled GCI quantum circuit for the one-risk-factor credit-risk model, including the replacement of the blue-box subcircuit with the experimentally tuned Gaussian-loading circuit.

algorithm.variant: hardware-ready transpiled Gaussian Conditional Independence circuit
algorithm.ansatz: 3-qubit circuit with Gaussian loading plus asset rotation and controlled operations
algorithm.optimizer: Qiskit preset pass manager with SABRE routing; later hardware-tuned pulse-level variational adjustment

key_results: Optimal hardware-ready parameters reported as theta3 = 90° and theta4 = 180°
The paper reports that the experimental and simulated CDFs agree within about 5% error
The 95% VaR is at total loss L = 1000 in both experimental and simulated hardware-ready transpiled circuits
Reported CDF values include P(L <= 0) ≈ 0.75 and P(L <= 1000) = 1.0
